title: scan_impl() collects all blocks into a Vec before returning — entire body must be scanned eagerly even if caller only wants first block
description: uuencoding/src/scan.rs scan_impl() scans the entire input and collects all results into a Vec<Result<ScannedBlock, UuError>>. The public scan() function in lib.rs wraps this with .into_iter(), which looks lazy but is actually eager: the full Vec is built before any item is consumed. For a large email body with 10 UU blocks, if the caller only wants the first, all 10 are decoded. The comment in scan_impl says 'non-lazy helper'. The public API promises an iterator but delivers fully-evaluated results. This is a documentation issue at minimum, and an efficiency issue for callers that break early.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) implement scan() as a true lazy iterator struct (more work, better API), or (b) document in the scan() doc comment that iteration is fully-eager and all blocks are decoded on the first call. If (b), consider renaming to make the eagerness obvious, or keep as-is with clear docs.
close_reason: Documented eager evaluation in scan() doc comment; noted that decode() is a lazy alternative
